8: Iteration 5 starts from the child's two BUB1B alleles and the BubR1 protein instead of from drug databases, in four routes run as one step, each licensed by a positive control declared in writing before the child's data were touched. R1 (allele-specific): the stop_gained allele's context was derived from the public gene model - a UGA stop with a +4 A in exon 17 of 23, 746 nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction, so nonsense-mediated decay destroys the message, and the entire protein-kinase domain is lost. A group-mean context model over 5,837 measured pathogenic premature stops x 8 compounds (Toledano 2024, PMID 39174735) predicts readthrough for this exact context; its held-out control (14 benchmark stops, plus a random fifth, bar rho >= 0.5 and pairwise ordering >= 0.7 fixed before the run) passes for 2,6-diaminopurine, G418 and SRI-41315, fails for five other compounds, and correctly fails for the untreated column. A dosage model then prices each lever in percent of wild-type BubR1: readthrough is worth at most about 1.4 points against a roughly 6.5-point gap, while doubling the missense protein is worth 12.5, so the missense allele is the lever and the aminoglycoside class is ruled out twice (predicted effect at the assay floor for this context, and nephrocalcinosis in the child's own terms). R2 (protein level): in drug-perturbation proteomics (Mitchell 2023, 875 compounds x 9,714 proteins; ProTargetMiner), BUB1B protein is 99.7th-percentile proliferation-bound, so a proliferation score is regressed out and the robust z of the residual ranked. The gating control (HSP90 inhibition raising HSPA1A) ranks 1 and 2 of 875. Five approved corrected risers move BubR1 by only 14-16 percent; the strongest raisers are a CDK1 inhibitor and a proteasome inhibitor, pointing at degradation. Re-running iteration 4's LINCS reversal with the cell-cycle component removed still fails its checkpoint-sibling control, so no reverser list was produced; TTK is the one sibling that survives. R3 (literature as a data source): 6 topic queries written without naming any paper retrieved 767 papers; a lexical screen selected sentences; a reader wrote structured intervention and exposure rows; then code, not the model, verified that every quoted sentence appears verbatim in the cached text of the cited paper. Recall 3/3 on both halves; 42 of 42 rows verified. R4 (decision and value of information): the three routes' 50 candidate rows are validated against a pinned schema, deduplicated on a normalised drug name and expanded over declared class analogues into 54 evidence rows over 45 distinct drugs, then scored in a utility table indexed by world-state. Two unmeasured facts define the world-states: whether the missense protein is unstable or inactive (prior 0.55/0.45, the register's triage weight from the stability atlas, whose own calibration says the predictor cannot separate the classes), and whether readthrough is feasible - a prior derived at run time from R1's own dosage table rather than typed in (0 of 9 real-dose pairs lift the child past the 13.0 percent segregation-fidelity threshold, so P(yes) = 0; 2 of 15 including R1's stated upper bounds). A drug's utility in a state is its best single argument (evidence strength x route weight x whether that branch acts in the state x a control factor that penalises a route whose control failed) times a per-child safety factor, with a 35-row avoid list - literature harm rows that lower BubR1, same-disease patient exposures, checkpoint-weakening classes, and the aminoglycosides against the child's nephrocalcinosis - driving three otherwise-proposed drugs to zero. Expected utility picks gliclazide tied with migalastat (0.385), against a baseline action 'defer; run the test first' that has utility 0 and wins ties. The route's output is not that ranking but the price of the next measurement: EVPI 0.180, of which EVPPI puts 0.180 on the missense question and 0.000 on readthrough; a cycloheximide-chase Western blot at an assumed 0.85/0.85 sensitivity and specificity has EVSI 0.106, 59 percent of that ceiling, and stays positive across every parameter range swept, while the recommended drug changes under three of them. The best action flips at P(unstable) 0.414, 0.14 below the configured prior. The route's positive control is a four-drug case small enough to work by hand, reproduced exactly (EU, EVPI 0.18, EVSI 0.096, flip at 0.36) by the test suite. Scalability was measured rather than asserted: R1-R3 were re-run unchanged on a second disease (Bloom syndrome, BLM) from case cards - 587 configuration lines plus 271 lines of one-time parameterisation, against a 378-line purpose-built driver for the same second disease in the previous iteration - with all nine first-case tables byte-identical afterwards, R1 additionally checked against a held-out published measurement of a BLM stop allele (Spearman 0.70 over nine compounds, p = 0.036, mean absolute error 0.41 percentage points, but up to 4x over-prediction for the two strongest compounds), and R3's declared control failing on that case (retrieval 3/3, extraction 0/3), so its rows are reported as uninterpretable.
9: Automated, with one human reading step that is gated by code. R1 and R2 are fully automated statistical pipelines over public datasets. R3 uses a language model to read screened sentences and write structured rows, but no row survives unless code finds its quoted sentence verbatim in the cached source text of the cited PMID; a failing row is rejected, never repaired. Drug mapping is automated against ChEMBL, with class analogues declared in a committed case card rather than inferred. No LLM ranked or selected drugs.
10: Manual work is limited and recorded. (a) In R3 the extraction step is a model reading 1,109 screened sentences and writing 42 structured rows; the judgement is which sentence is a finding and what it says, and the quote gate is the check on it. (b) The class analogues that turn a tool compound or a genetic experiment into an approved drug (for example trichostatin A to the approved HDAC inhibitors) are declared by hand in tools/it5_litmine_params.py so a reader can argue with them. (c) R1's dosage inputs (message survival, protein fold-reduction, specific activity) are read from named papers and stated as assumptions with their PMIDs. (d) The report wording is written by hand from the entries. No candidate was added or removed by hand.
11: Publicly available sources only. No proprietary data source was used.
12: Toledano, Supek and Lehner, Nature Genetics 2024 (PMID 39174735) supplementary table 3, 5,837 measured premature termination codons x 8 compounds; Ensembl REST release 116 (GRCh38) and UniProt O60566 for the BUB1B gene model and domains; Mitchell 2023, Nature Biotechnology 41:845 (PMID 36593396) supplementary data 3, drug-perturbation proteomics in HCT116; Saei 2019, Nature Communications 10:5715 (PMID 31844049) ProTargetMiner deep sets; Nusinow 2020 CCLE protein quantification; Mathieson 2018 protein half-lives; the Tirosh 2016 cell-cycle gene sets (PMID 27124452) as shipped by Seurat; LINCS L1000 2021 CRISPR-knockout consensus and the CMap LINCS 2020 beta gene table; Europe PMC search and full-text XML; ChEMBL and openFDA drug labels for approval evidence; ClinVar and gnomAD for the stop allele's annotation; the proband's 8 HPO terms from the challenge's clinical file. Every downloaded file's sha256 and URL are recorded in the table manifests under ressources/track2/it5/.
14: Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a compound heterozygote confirmed by the challenge's answer key: one stop_gained and one missense allele in BUB1B. Iteration 5 characterises the two alleles separately. The stop allele is a UGA premature termination codon with a +4 A in exon 17 of 23, 746 nucleotides upstream of the last exon-exon junction, therefore competent for nonsense-mediated decay: its message is destroyed and no truncated protein accumulates, and the truncation would in any case remove the entire protein-kinase domain (UniProt 766-1050). It is effectively a null. The missense allele keeps a normal message and, in published MVA patient cells, a protein present at a two- to six-fold reduced level whose activity is restored by forced overexpression, so the functional deficit is one of protein amount rather than protein quality - the hypomorphic half of the genotype. Pathway disrupted: the spindle assembly checkpoint, in which BubR1 is part of the mitotic checkpoint complex. Downstream consequence: chromosome mis-segregation and mosaic aneuploidy, with early senescence, muscle wasting and growth failure in the corresponding mouse hypomorph, matching the child's clinical terms. The fork iteration 5 cannot close from public data is whether the missense protein is unstable (degraded fast) or inactive (stable but broken); a cycloheximide-chase measurement in patient cells separates them.
15: Iteration 5's step 1 ran on 2026-09-25 on a laptop, in four routes, at 0 USD of compute and with no GPU. Approximate wall-clock per route: R1 about 10 minutes of downloads plus seconds of fitting; R2 about 10 minutes of downloads, 90 seconds for the proteome run and 13 seconds for the LINCS control; R3 about an hour, most of it Europe PMC retrieval of 767 papers and 1,065 texts. R4 adds no download at all - it reads the three committed candidate tables and reuses the cached PharmCAT output and the local OnSIDES label copy - and its run, figures and test suite complete in seconds; no stopwatch figure was recorded for it, so none is quoted. The transfer check to the second disease was timed and is reported exactly: R1 6.1 s, R2 12.5 s, R3 738 s of which 702 s is network-bound Europe PMC retrieval, about 12.6 minutes in total, plus the model's own reading time for the screened sentences, which is agent time and is reported separately in the entry rather than folded into the machine time.
16:
Question. A child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy carries a confirmed compound-heterozygous BUB1B genotype: one stop_gained allele and one missense allele. Earlier iterations asked drug databases what to give him and got answers at chance level. Iteration 5 asks instead: given these two alleles and the BubR1 protein, which therapeutic route exists per allele, and what would the next measurement be worth?

Approach. Four routes, run as one step. No hypotheses were pre-registered in the science register - a recorded decision, and a real weakness, because a positive control does not rule out steering the analysis after seeing the data. In its place each route declared a positive control in writing before the child's data were touched, and a route whose control fails is reported as uninterpretable rather than argued around. Two of the six controls in this work failed, and both failures are reported: the cell-cycle-corrected LINCS reversal, and route R3 re-run on the second disease.

Results. R1 reads the stop allele with a context model fitted to 5,837 measured premature stops: it is NMD-competent and loses the entire kinase domain, and a dosage arithmetic prices even a perfect readthrough agent at about +1.4 percentage points of working BubR1 against a roughly 6.5-point gap, while doubling the missense protein is worth +12.5 - so the missense allele, not the stop, is the lever. R2 scores 875 compounds on protein rather than mRNA, regressing out proliferation first because BUB1B sits in the 99.7th percentile of proliferation-bound proteins: only five approved compounds raise it, by 14-16 percent, and the strongest raisers are a CDK1 and a proteasome inhibitor, pointing at degradation. R3 mines the literature with a code-enforced quote gate - no row survives unless its quoted sentence is a verbatim substring of the cached source - yielding 30 verified intervention rows (NAD+ precursors, HDAC inhibitors, proteasome inhibitors, hypomethylating agents, senolytics) and 12 exposure rows recording what MVA patients were actually given - 42 rows in all, 0 rejected, and the gate itself mutation-tested. R4 weighs the three against the two unmeasured facts and prices the gap instead of guessing it: EVPI 0.180, all of it on whether the missense protein is unstable or inactive and none on readthrough; a cycloheximide-chase blot captures 0.106, 59 percent of that ceiling, and is positive across every range swept, while the top-ranked drug flips under three separate assumptions.

Strengths and limits. Allele-level mechanism, a declared control per route, a code-enforced quote gate, a direction-aware avoid list, full provenance with input digests, case-agnostic modules re-run on a second disease with byte-identical first-case outputs, zero compute cost. Nothing was measured in this child; the evidence comes from cancer cell lines, mice and papers; protein amount is not protein function; every utility and prior is a stated weight and not a calibrated probability; no row is treatment advice. The deliverable is a measurement and an avoid list, not a prescription.
